findings.title: Hardcoded AWS access keys in provider config, Lambda env, and EC2 user-data
findings.attack_path: Long-lived AKIA access keys and secret keys are committed in plaintext in providers.tf (plain_text_access_keys_provider), lambda.tf environment variables, and EC2 user-data (ec2.tf). Anyone with repo read access, anyone who can read the Lambda config, or anyone who reads instance user-data via IMDS harvests valid static credentials and authenticates directly to AWS, bypassing all network controls.
findings.remediation: Remove all hardcoded keys. Use IAM roles / instance profiles / IRSA and an AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store reference instead of static keys. Rotate and revoke any exposed key immediately and scrub git history.

findings.title: RDS MySQL instance publicly accessible with weak hardcoded admin password
findings.attack_path: aws_db_instance.default sets publicly_accessible=true with username admin and a default password (Aa1234321Bb in consts.tf, also embedded in EC2 user-data). The DB endpoint is reachable from outside the VPC; an attacker brute-forces or simply reuses the committed password to log in and read/modify the EMPLOYEES data over :3306.
findings.remediation: Set publicly_accessible=false, place RDS in private subnets, source the password from Secrets Manager with auto-rotation, and enforce a strong unique credential. Restrict the security group to the app tier only.

findings.title: Security group exposes SSH (22) and HTTP (80) to 0.0.0.0/0
findings.attack_path: aws_security_group.web-node opens ports 22 and 80 to 0.0.0.0/0 (ec2.tf). The whole internet can scan and reach SSH; combined with the instance profile granting s3:*/ec2:*/rds:*, a successful SSH compromise yields broad account access and lateral movement.
findings.remediation: Restrict ingress to known admin CIDRs or move SSH behind SSM Session Manager / a bastion. Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 SSH rule; front HTTP with the load balancer only.

findings.title: Over-permissive IAM policies grant wildcard actions on all resources
findings.attack_path: The EC2 instance role policy (db-app.tf) grants s3:*/ec2:*/rds:* on Resource * and the IAM user excess_policy (iam.tf) grants ec2:*/s3:*/lambda:*/cloudwatch:* on *. Any compromise of the instance, its IMDS credentials, or the user's access key yields near-admin control with no blast-radius limit.
findings.remediation: Replace wildcards with least-privilege actions scoped to specific ARNs. Split duties across roles and add permission boundaries / SCPs.

findings.title: Elasticsearch domain access policy allows es:* to AWS principal * with no encryption or VPC
findings.attack_path: es.tf attaches an access policy with actions es:*, principal AWS=* on resources *, and the domain has no VPC, no node-to-node encryption, and no encryption at rest. Any AWS principal (effectively any anonymous caller against a public endpoint) can read, write, or delete indexed monitoring data.
findings.remediation: Scope the access policy to specific principals and source IPs, deploy the domain inside a VPC, enable encryption at rest and node-to-node encryption, and upgrade off Elasticsearch 2.3.

findings.title: S3 data bucket holding customer-master.xlsx is public/unencrypted with no logging or versioning
findings.attack_path: aws_s3_bucket.data is created with no public-access block, no server-side encryption, no access logging, and no versioning (s3.tf), and it stores resources/customer-master.xlsx. A misconfigured/public ACL exposes restricted customer data for download with no audit trail and no ability to recover from tampering or deletion.
findings.remediation: Enable S3 Block Public Access, default SSE-KMS encryption, access logging, and versioning. Apply a restrictive bucket policy and classify the contents as RESTRICTED.

findings.title: Sensitive S3 buckets lack encryption, logging, and versioning
findings.attack_path: financials, operations, and data_science buckets (s3.tf) are unencrypted; financials and operations also have no access logging, and financials has no versioning. An attacker with any read access exfiltrates plaintext financial/operational data and the gap in logging hides the access.
findings.remediation: Enable default SSE-KMS on every bucket, turn on access logging to the logs bucket, and enable versioning with lifecycle/MFA-delete on data-bearing buckets.

findings.title: RDS, Neptune, EBS volume/snapshot, and VPC flow-log bucket are unencrypted at rest
findings.attack_path: storage_encrypted=false on the RDS instance (db-app.tf) and Neptune cluster (neptune.tf); the EBS volume and its snapshot are unencrypted (ec2.tf); the flow-log bucket has no SSE. An attacker with snapshot-copy or storage-layer access reads data in cleartext, and shared/exported snapshots leak data across accounts.
findings.remediation: Set storage_encrypted=true with KMS CMKs on RDS and Neptune, enable EBS encryption (and encrypted snapshots), and add SSE to the flow-log bucket.

findings.title: ELB serves traffic over cleartext HTTP with no TLS termination
findings.attack_path: aws_elb.weblb listens on HTTP :80 forwarding to instance HTTP :8000 (elb.tf) with no HTTPS listener or certificate. The PHP form submits NAME/ADDRESS in cleartext; an on-path attacker reads or modifies submitted data and session content.
findings.remediation: Add an HTTPS listener with an ACM certificate, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, and migrate to an Application Load Balancer with a modern TLS policy.

findings.title: PHP web app stored input rendered to all users without output encoding (stored XSS)
findings.attack_path: The user-data PHP app (db-app.tf) inserts POSTed NAME/ADDRESS into the EMPLOYEES table and later echoes query_data[1]/[2] directly into the HTML table with no output encoding on render. A stored payload submitted via the public form executes in the browser of every later viewer, including any privileged operator reviewing the page.
findings.remediation: HTML-encode all stored values on output (htmlspecialchars), add a Content-Security-Policy, and validate input server-side. Treat the page as untrusted multi-user output.

findings.title: EOL runtimes and base image (Node.js 12.x Lambda, python:3.7-slim, Elasticsearch 2.3)
findings.attack_path: lambda.tf pins runtime nodejs12.x (EOL), resources/Dockerfile uses python:3.7-slim (EOL), and es.tf runs Elasticsearch 2.3. Unpatched runtime/library CVEs in these components give an attacker known exploit paths with no vendor fixes available.
findings.remediation: Upgrade Lambda to a supported Node.js runtime, rebuild on a supported Python base image, and move to a current OpenSearch version. Add dependency/image scanning to CI.

findings.title: ECR repository allows mutable tags with no image scanning
findings.attack_path: aws_ecr_repository.repository sets image_tag_mutability=MUTABLE with no scan_on_push (ecr.tf), and the null_resource provisioner builds/pushes via local-exec. An attacker who can push overwrites a trusted tag with a malicious image that downstream consumers pull, and vulnerable images are never flagged.
findings.remediation: Set image_tag_mutability=IMMUTABLE, enable scan_on_push, and require signed images (e.g., cosign) before deployment.

findings.title: EKS cluster lacks private-only endpoint, control-plane logging, and secrets encryption
findings.attack_path: aws_eks_cluster.eks_cluster enables endpoint_private_access but does not disable public access, has no enabled_cluster_log_types, no KMS envelope encryption for secrets, and its nodes sit in public subnets (eks.tf). The API is reachable from the internet and control-plane activity is unlogged, easing reconnaissance and undetected control-plane abuse.
findings.remediation: Disable public endpoint access (or restrict public CIDRs), enable all control-plane log types, enable KMS secrets encryption, and place worker nodes in private subnets.

findings.title: RDS/Neptune backups disabled or minimal; deletion protection and final snapshots skipped
findings.attack_path: aws_db_instance.default sets backup_retention_period=0 and skip_final_snapshot=true (db-app.tf), one Aurora cluster has backup_retention_period=0 (rds.tf), and Neptune sets skip_final_snapshot=true (neptune.tf). An attacker or operator who deletes a cluster destroys data with no recovery point, and there is no deletion protection.
findings.remediation: Set a non-zero backup_retention_period, enable deletion_protection, disable skip_final_snapshot, and enforce backup policies organization-wide.

findings.title: IAM user with long-lived static access key instead of role-based access
findings.attack_path: iam.tf creates an aws_iam_user plus an aws_iam_access_key and outputs the username/secret. A long-lived programmatic credential paired with the wildcard excess_policy is a durable, exfiltratable key that grants broad account access if it leaks (Terraform state, CI logs, outputs).
findings.remediation: Eliminate the static user; use IAM roles with short-lived STS credentials (IRSA / instance profiles / OIDC federation). If a user is unavoidable, scope its policy and rotate keys automatically.

findings.title: KMS key for log bucket has rotation disabled with short deletion window
findings.attack_path: aws_kms_key.logs_key omits enable_key_rotation (defaults to disabled) and uses a 7-day deletion window (kms.tf). Without rotation, a single compromised key version exposes all historical log data; a short deletion window lets an attacker schedule key deletion and render KMS-encrypted logs unrecoverable.
findings.remediation: Set enable_key_rotation=true, increase deletion_window_in_days to 30, and apply a key policy restricting kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion.

findings.title: Terraform S3 state backend lacks DynamoDB locking and KMS CMK; secrets land in state
findings.attack_path: providers.tf configures backend s3 with encrypt=true but no KMS CMK and no dynamodb_table for state locking. The DB password, IAM access-key secret, and other sensitive outputs are written to remote state; without locking, concurrent applies corrupt state, and read access to the state bucket discloses all secrets in cleartext-equivalent form.
findings.remediation: Add a dedicated KMS CMK to the backend, configure dynamodb_table for locking, restrict the state bucket with Block Public Access and a tight policy, and keep secrets out of outputs.
